rationale: The guideline fixes Finance at half the company card and leaves no range — the one row in the table with nothing to negotiate.
A quarter to the customer aspect keeps the card from becoming a P&L with extra steps.
The floor. Processes at company level is oversight of the blocks that own it, not the work itself.
Half again the processes weight, because the company card is the only level where the headcount plan is decided.
Heaviest Finance weight in the table. A block that touches revenue directly is scored on revenue.
The customer is in front of them, so the aspect is real work rather than a proxy — but it stays below Finance.
The floor again. Front office follows process; it does not own it.
Lightest People weight anywhere in the table, and the row that makes the low end of this block sum to 95%.
Half the front-office weight. Manufacturing affects cost and margin without owning the sale.
Their customer is often the front office, which is why this aspect can outweigh Finance here.
Where process stops being oversight and becomes the job.
Skilled work with a training cost, so People carries more than it does out front.
Lowest Finance weight. A block with no revenue line scored heavily on revenue is being scored on somebody else's work.
Their customer is internal. The aspect survives because internal service is still service.
Widest range in the table, and the heaviest ceiling. Back office is where process is the product.
Half a card at the ceiling. HR and admin own the People aspect, so it can dominate theirs.
